[Osamu Sakura](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/22/doc/24013/Sakura_at_GAITC.jpg)

佐倉　統 Osamu Sakura

廣電系邀請日本學者佐倉　統（Osamu Sakura）教授，於 2023 年 9 月 1 日至 2023 年 12 月 29 日至本校傳播學院廣播電視學系擔任訪問學者。

Dr. Osamu Sakura is a Professor of Interfaculty Initiative in Information Studies, the University of Tokyo, and PI of Research Project for Science, Technology and Society, RIKEN Center for Advanced Intelligence Project (AIP), Japan. His main interests are science and technology studies, including social aspects of AI and robotics, comparative history of the reception of evolutionary theory, and cultural effects on the history of science and technology in Japan. He was also engaged in the relationship between experts and local people in the evacuation areas of the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster. Having got a Ph.D. from Kyoto University, Japan, in primatology and behavioral ecology, he taught at Yokohama National University (1993-2000) and worked as visiting scholar at the University of Freiburg (1995-96) before moving to his current position in 2000. He published several journal papers and books.

sakura@iii.u-tokyo.ac.jp

Research and Teaching Experience

1993-2000   Associate Professor, Faculty of Business Administration, Yokohama National University

1995-1996   Visiting Researcher, Institut für Informatik und Gesellschaft, Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg, Germany

2000-Present   Associate Professor (2000-07), Professor (2007-present), Dean (2015-18), Interfaculty Initiative in Information Studies, The University of Tokyo

2012   Visiting Scholar, National Core for Neuroethics, University of British Columbia, Canda

2017-Present    Team Leader, Science, Technology and Society Research Team, RIKEN Center for Integrated Research on Innovative Intelligence (AIP)

Fields of Research

Science and technology studies (STS), Science and technology communication, Neuroethics, AI and society

[Dr. Tets Kimura](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/22/doc/29377/Dr. Tets Kimura.jpg)

Dr. Tets Kimura

廣電系邀請澳洲 Flinders 大學之博士後研究員 Dr. Tets Kimura 先生來臺，研究期間為 113 年 8 月至 10 月，共計 3 個月。

福林德斯大學文創藝術系兼任講師。

為學者、作家、記者與翻譯家，研究專長為藝術和文化史、時尚研究、亞洲／日本研究和國際關係。

Education

Flinders University and the University of South Australia, supplemented by coursework completed at the University of East Anglia (UK) and Pukyong National University (South Korea).

Proficiency & Experiences

Professionally bilingual, Dr. Kimura holds a [NAATI](https://www.naati.com.au/) qualification for translation / interpreting between English and Japanese. He offers his expertise as a Japanese language interpreter for governmental sectors, private organisations, and the media industry. Currently, he is studying Chinese in his spare time.

With an extensive teaching background, Dr. Kimura has shared his expertise internationally at institutions like [Flinders University](https://researchnow.flinders.edu.au/en/persons/tets-kimura) (Australia), Fukuoka Women’s University (Japan), and National Chengchi University (Taiwan).

As a journalist, Dr. Kimura reported from Baghdad in 2004 and covered the last five Australian federal elections for the Japanese Mainichi national newspaper.

Dr. Kimura’s involvement includes creating English subtitles for internationally-acclaimed Japanese director Kuro Tanino’s [The Dark Master](https://www.japanesestudies.org.uk/ejcjs/vol21/iss1/kimura_tanino.html) at the 2019 OzAsia Festival and curating an exhibition of art by Japanese internees from Australasian camps at the Showa no Kurashi Museum in Tokyo in 2022.

Currently, he is diligently working on his upcoming book based on his paper presented at the European Association for Japanese Studies (EAJS) Conference (The End of Fashion Conference) in Japan entitled Fashion, Soft Power, and Cultural Diplomacy: A Case Study of Japanese Fashion in Australia.

日期：2020-02-12

[廣電營](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/22/doc/1683/_archive_1076_174f88dc.jpg)

籌辦給全國高中生的暑假營隊，旨在提供還未踏入社會的青年學子，一個更了解廣播與電視領域的機會。雖是學生活動，但課程內容絕對不馬虎，營隊期間，將邀請各領域專精老師或是傑出系友授課，囊括入門的傳播概要、影像與廣播的介紹與實作方法，以及電視與廣播產業的講解，還會參訪電視台和廣播電視台，讓學生對該領域的工作環境有更直接的認識。課程之外，還有精彩的表演和特色團康，學習之餘絕無冷場

精華的五天四夜，不管是對廣電系本身，還是參加者，都是一個盡情揮灑自我、展現創意的絕佳體驗。

[系所簡介系所設備2](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/upload/22/doc/1878/系所簡介系所設備2.jpg)

Center for Media and Information

The Center for Media and Information was founded in 2003, and integrates all of the teaching, application, and experiment resources of the College of Communication. There are six divisions: the VNCCU radio station, IT Lab, Audio-Video Lab, Theater, News Lab and Research Oriented Media Lab. The Center plans all human resources and budgets to coordinate the demands of teaching, research and application, thus boosting the competitive advantages of the College.

About Communication Library

The communication library, known as “News Material Room” was founded in 1962. It was located on the third level of college of Journalism, mainly to provide professional communication archives for faculties and students. This was the only professional journalism library in Taiwan back then.

The Chiang Kai-shek Library started operating in 1977, the “News Material Room”  belongs to Chung Cheng Library Reading Section, and the library sent its own personnel to help manage it.

The school of communication was established in 1990, Reading Section then moved from third level of department of Journalism to nowadays location, which is the third floor of the college of communication. Its area is 113 pyeong, and the name was changed to “The library of college of communication”. Up until 1993, the name officially became “Communication Library ”.

In 2007, the school asked Professor Yo, Ben Kuan from the department of advertising to help coloring design, hardware management, and the spacing adjustment so that “Communication Library ” will present a new atmosphere. The library collections include professional western written books, both east and western journals, newspapers, visual-aid information, and doctors’ research papers. It is the library that has the largest collections that are related to communication professionals.

Voice of NCCU 

VNCCU is the College’s student radio station, with a long history and outstanding student-produced programming. By focusing on the ins and outs of campus life and the unique character of the Wen-Shan District, the station’s programming is broadly accessible and serves as a model for caring for the campus. The station has also established a website that allows audiences to listen at their convenience. For the most up-to-date information on the Wen-Shan District and life at NCCU, tune in to FM 88.7.

Audio-Video Lab 

The student-operated AV Lab offers audio-video production classes, facility lending, and research support. It also provides students with comprehensive support, to ensure that they can successfully film or direct their audio-video projects. The AV Lab also offers live and on-demand broadcasts of academic events, campus activities, student projects, and educational programming, to highlight the university’s achievements.

Theater of Communication College 

Small but complete, this professional theater provides students with a performance space and venue for drama productions and large-scale outdoor performances. The student-run theater also holds classes for using theater equipment and acting skills, and hosts performances by numerous theater companies.

ITLab 

The ITLab provides the basic IT services to the College’s students and faculty, such as the software/photography workshops and maintaining the computing hardware facilities. ITLab also trains students in information design and photography, and highlights students’ creativity by displaying their multimedia works at the end of every semester. The main goal is to awaken students’ powers of observation and creativity, and improving their production skills.

News Lab 

Students handle everything from reporting, writing, and editing to taking photographs, thus delivering a student perspective on current affairs in our ever-changing world. The work that students do here serves to broaden their worldview and hone their writing skills. For the digital media age, the Uonline system has also introduced audio/video content and online interactivity, to liven its presentation of the news.

Research-Oriented Media Lab 

Designed to simulate an ordinary living space, the lab integrates research, demonstration and academic-industrial cooperation facilities in a new setting that allows researchers to observe users’ media consumption behaviors first-hand.

Date 2026-08-10

 

NCCU Radio and Television Department to Present 2026 Graduation Showcase, In the Unfinished Between 

The Department of Radio and Television at National Chengchi University (NCCU) will present its 2026 Independent Project Graduation Showcase, In the Unfinished Between, in June.

Continuing the department’s longstanding tradition of creative practice, this year’s showcase is independently curated by students and brings together diverse works in moving image, music, theatre, game design and audiovisual production. The exhibition highlights graduating students’ four years of exploration and practice in media, storytelling and contemporary issues.

The showcase consists of two main components: a Production Exhibition and a Film Festival.

The Production Exhibition will take place from June 3 to June 7, 2026, at the Exhibition Hall of NCCU’s Journalism Building. It will feature 10 projects across four categories: music, moving image, theatre and game design.

The Film Festival will be held on June 11 and 12 at the second-floor theatre of NCCU’s College of Communication. On June 14, three narrative films and one documentary will be screened at the Audiovisual Hall of NCCU’s Arts and Culture Center. An online film festival is also scheduled to take place on YouTube from June 20 to June 21, allowing a wider audience to participate in the exchange.

Titled In the Unfinished Between, the exhibition focuses on the uncertainty and fluctuation experienced by contemporary young people between becoming and not becoming, leaving and staying, and dreams and reality.

The curatorial concept suggests that people do not simply pause briefly in the process of making choices; instead, they may live for extended periods in a state of incompleteness. Unfinished decisions, unrealized ideals and futures that remain out of reach have gradually become part of everyday contemporary experience.

Rather than offering answers to struggle, In the Unfinished Between examines how struggle continues to exist. Here, “between” is no longer merely a transitional stage, but a condition in which one resides. Likewise, “unfinished” is no longer defined solely as absence or deficiency; it becomes a shared reality of life for contemporary youth.

Through different media and creative forms, the exhibition seeks to open a dialogue between the works and their audiences. Visitors are invited to reconsider their own positions and directions amid states of uncertainty and incompletion.

The event welcomes students in communication, radio and television, film and related fields, as well as all audiences interested in student productions and short films. Visitors are invited to enter In the Unfinished Between and experience the creative energy and life questions of contemporary youth.

[2026-08-10NCCU Radio and Television Department to Present 2026 Graduation Showcase, In the Unfinished BetweenNCCU Radio and Television Department to Present 2026 Graduation Showcase, In the Unfinished Between 

The Department of Radio and Television at National Chengchi University (NCCU) will present its 2026 Independent Project Graduation Showcase, In the Unfinished Between, in June.

Continuing the department’s longstanding tradition of creative practice, this year’s showcase is independently curated by students and brings together diverse works in moving image, music, theatre, game design and audiovisual production. The exhibition highlights graduating students’ four years of exploration and practice in media, storytelling and contemporary issues.

The showcase consists of two main components: a Production Exhibition and a Film Festival.

The Production Exhibition will take place from June 3 to June 7, 2026, at the Exhibition Hall of NCCU’s Journalism Building. It will feature 10 projects across four categories: music, moving image, theatre and game design.

The Film Festival will be held on June 11 and 12 at the second-floor theatre of NCCU’s College of Communication. On June 14, three narrative films and one documentary will be screened at the Audiovisual Hall of NCCU’s Arts and Culture Center. An online film festival is also scheduled to take place on YouTube from June 20 to June 21, allowing a wider audience to participate in the exchange.

Titled In the Unfinished Between, the exhibition focuses on the uncertainty and fluctuation experienced by contemporary young people between becoming and not becoming, leaving and staying, and dreams and reality.

The curatorial concept suggests that people do not simply pause briefly in the process of making choices; instead, they may live for extended periods in a state of incompleteness. Unfinished decisions, unrealized ideals and futures that remain out of reach have gradually become part of everyday contemporary experience.

Rather than offering answers to struggle, In the Unfinished Between examines how struggle continues to exist. Here, “between” is no longer merely a transitional stage, but a condition in which one resides. Likewise, “unfinished” is no longer defined solely as absence or deficiency; it becomes a shared reality of life for contemporary youth.

Through different media and creative forms, the exhibition seeks to open a dialogue between the works and their audiences. Visitors are invited to reconsider their own positions and directions amid states of uncertainty and incompletion.

The event welcomes students in communication, radio and television, film and related fields, as well as all audiences interested in student productions and short films. Visitors are invited to enter In the Unfinished Between and experience the creative energy and life questions of contemporary youth.](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDocAll/Detail?fid=4839&id=42154)

Introduction

itroduction

多國語

Given the need of developing communication technologies and professions of radio and television, National Chengchi University (NCCU) set up the first School of Radio and Television among Taiwan universities in 1987 and started to enroll in 1988 upon the approval of the Ministry of Education. Since 1992, NCCU started to develop the graduate degree program. In three years, NCCU established full graduate institutes and started to enroll the next year. The university became the first to have Radio and Television Master program in the nation to nurture professions and academic researches in radio and television.

With the need of professions in communication, the department of journalism, advertising, and radio and television started to enroll students as undecided major in the College of Communication for their freshman and sophomore years, and have their major confirmed in their junior year since 2014 academic year. The College of Communication provides two programs: Media Innovation and Management and Audiovisual Media Design and Production. Starting from the 2014 academic year, the original Master program of journalism, advertising and radio and television integrated as College of Communication Master Program. Students would be able to have the freedom to choose their courses and develop themselves based on their potentials.

Up till 2025, our department has 13 full-time professors including 5 professors, 5 associate professors, 3 assistant professors, and several part-time professors; and around 150 undergraduate students.

The professors in our department have been responsible in teaching, researching and attending the University, Colleges, and Department’s administration work. Our department has been widely acclaimed for our teaching, researches and services. In order to share our research to the academia and industries, we have held integration of academic and practical conferences since 1991 and started printing academic journal, Radio and Television since July 1992.

The mission of Department of Radio and Television has been: “developing students’ humanism quality, critical thinking, creativity and international perspective.” Our department has been committed to recruit qualify teachers, substantial hardware facilities to achieve quality teaching environment, promote academic researches and activities and nurtures innovation and scholarly development in radio, television and new media management.

The goal of National Chengchi University Department of Radio and Television is to nurture students with humanities, critical thinking, creativities and global perspectives in order to prepare them for the diverse digital media and have the ability to integrate video with multimedia communication professions. Throughout the years, we encourage students to take foreign language as second major to increase their ability of foreign language speaking. We also provide overseas exchange program for students to broaden their horizons. As to expend our Department, we sincerely invite our students and alumni to translate this introduction into other languages for the world to see!

Educational Goals for Graduates

For graduates, the educational goals are to refine students’ self-discipline, critical thinking, and creativity. Furthermore, we aim to enhance our students’ ability to produce content for mass media, multicultural contexts, and effective communication. The Department of Radio & Television programs not only encourages students to hone their skills but also to develop international perspectives and leadership qualities.

Enhance students’ proficiency in electronic media production skills and foster innovative creativity.

Deepen students’ knowledge of electronic media content production and management.

Strengthen students’ abilities in electronic media management.

Broaden students’ understanding of electronic media regulations, historical development, and social impact.

Develop students’ teaching abilities.

Master’s Program Curriculum

In view of departmental integration within the College of Communication, the master’s Programs in “Journalism,” “Advertising” and “Radio & Television” have been reconstituted into the “Master’s Program of Communication” starting from the 2014 academic year. The program curriculum has been designed to integrate educational resources within the College, to expand and innovate existing fields of knowledge, and to provide advanced training for young professionals who are preparing to enter the communications industry. To better address industry trends and provide students with a more comprehensive learning environment, the program will be offering a wide range of highly specialized academic courses in seven concentrations: “Communications and Culture,” “Journalism and Communication,” “Imagination, Narrative, and Interaction,” “Telecommunication Policy and Management,” “Integrated Communication,” “Science and Risk Communication,” and “China Studies in Communication.” Students are also encouraged to engage in self-directed learning by designing their own curriculum on condition of receiving the approval of their academic advisors as well as the College of Communication.

The master’s program is structured around concentrations, with students choosing their own concentration in their first year. Once they’ve completed the College’s requirements, core curriculum, and requirements for their concentration, students can register for seminars of their choice. The Master's Program of Communication jointly offer seven primary concentrations, as well as an online master’s programs in international communications that provides professional development to individuals already working in the field.

For details, please see the most recent edition of the College’s course catalog for master’s students. For internship information, please click [here](http://comm.nccu.edu.tw/?locale=en).

E-mail: [gradcomm@nccu.edu.tw](mailto:gradcomm@nccu.edu.tw)

Tel: +886-2-2938-7123

Concentrations

Communication and Cultures

The program emphasizes cross-disciplinary research aimed at exploring, analyzing, and studying the mechanisms and results of interactions between communications media and other fields. The program helps students develop a solid background in theory and research, making it a good fit for those who plan to pursue Ph.D.s

Journalism, Information & Communication Program

The program trains students in reporting and writing, storytelling, and cross-media production, building fundamental skills in idea generation, composition, information gathering, and presentation. The program also places great emphasis on the development of professional ethics.

Imagination, Narratives, and Interactivity Program

The program trains professionals to produce content for traditional and emerging forms of new media. It teaches students fundamental and advanced production skills, and hones their ability to think creatively, critically, and independently. It also seeks to broaden students’ understanding of the humanities and the arts in order to add depth to their work and provide them with a background in narrative theory.

Telecommunications Policy and Management Program

The program explores the media ecology and investigates its evolution from the standpoint of policy and administration. Responding to the growth of the industry as whole, the program also draws on information from related fields. Its objective is to provide students with a broad, well-informed perspective, as well as the ability to analyze both the internal management structures and the external environment of the communications, telecommunications, and Internet industries.

Integrated Communications Program

The program deepens students’ understanding of the theory and practical application of advertising and public relations. It also provides students with the opportunity to meet and interact with professionals in the aesthetic and design industries by arranging seminars on digital content, arts management, experiential marketing, aesthetic economics, and the creative and cultural industries.

China Studies in Communications

Because Taiwan and China, are geographical close and in regular contact, studies in communication are becoming a distinct research field to explore. This program has been developed by our graduate institute to extend our research on communication to a new level, based on studies research in the Chinese-speaking world. We also aim to integrate communication studies with other disciplines, thus creating invaluable resources for our college and other specialties at the university. Students will be trained in observation of and research on the communication phenomena in the Chinese-speaking world, especially in Taiwan and China. Professionals who are required to understand the current situation of communication across the Strait are also welcome.

Science and Risk Communication

This program is developed to cultivate specialists in communication and the media, and who have a full understanding of contemporary science and its risks. Students receive both theoretical and practical training across different disciplines.

Interdisciplinary Program

The program allows students to design a personalized and interdisciplinary course of study not subject to the limitations of the core curriculum.

Curriculum Map (applicable to Class of Academic Year 115 therefrom)

Curriculum Map (applicable to Class of Academic Year 109 therefrom)

Our educational goals for undergraduates are to enhance students’ self-discipline, critical thinking, and creativity. Additionally, we aim to improve our students’ proficiency in media production according to international trends, social skills, and general education.

Educational Goals for Undergraduates

Develop students’ proficiency in traditional media production skills.

Conducting interviews, writing, editing, and broadcasting news

Producing cultural and educational content

Creating reality and documentary content

Developing drama and cinema content

Enhance students’ knowledge of electronic media content production and management.

Foster students’ understanding of electronic media’s evolution, regulations and policies, and social impact.

Cultivate students’ sense of teamwork, service, and responsibility.

“Curriculum Map applicable to Class of Academic Year 115” applies to undergraduate students admitted in the Academic Year 115 therefrom and to students approved for a double major in the Department of Radio and Television during the Academic Year 115 therefrom.

“Culture Cup” Choir Competition of National Chengchi University was found in 12 December 1968. For the students in Department of Radio and Television, “Culture Cup” Choir Competition is one of the major activities to bond their friendship. Most of the students are freshmen and sophomores. Juniors and seniors would attend with interest and their availabilities. The Department of Radio and Television sees this competition as a performance, and they even make the record of ten times consecutive champion. Students are willing to challenge themselves in different genre of songs, train themselves and give surprises to the audiences. All members in the department work hard together, sing happily, and share their joy and touching moments.

[2026-02-022024Visiting ProfessorDr. Tets Kimura

廣電系邀請澳洲 Flinders 大學之博士後研究員 Dr. Tets Kimura 先生來臺，研究期間為 113 年 8 月至 10 月，共計 3 個月。

	
	福林德斯大學文創藝術系兼任講師。
	
	
	為學者、作家、記者與翻譯家，研究專長為藝術和文化史、時尚研究、亞洲／日本研究和國際關係。
	

Education

Flinders University and the University of South Australia, supplemented by coursework completed at the University of East Anglia (UK) and Pukyong National University (South Korea).

Proficiency & Experiences

Professionally bilingual, Dr. Kimura holds a NAATI qualification for translation / interpreting between English and Japanese. He offers his expertise as a Japanese language interpreter for governmental sectors, private organisations, and the media industry. Currently, he is studying Chinese in his spare time.

With an extensive teaching background, Dr. Kimura has shared his expertise internationally at institutions like Flinders University (Australia), Fukuoka Women’s University (Japan), and National Chengchi University (Taiwan).

As a journalist, Dr. Kimura reported from Baghdad in 2004 and covered the last five Australian federal elections for the Japanese Mainichi national newspaper.

Dr. Kimura’s involvement includes creating English subtitles for internationally-acclaimed Japanese director Kuro Tanino’s The Dark Master at the 2019 OzAsia Festival and curating an exhibition of art by Japanese internees from Australasian camps at the Showa no Kurashi Museum in Tokyo in 2022.

Currently, he is diligently working on his upcoming book based on his paper presented at the European Association for Japanese Studies (EAJS) Conference (The End of Fashion Conference) in Japan entitled Fashion, Soft Power, and Cultural Diplomacy: A Case Study of Japanese Fashion in Australia.

[2023-08-302023Visiting Professor佐倉　統 　Osamu Sakura

廣電系邀請日本學者佐倉 統（Osamu Sakura）教授，於 2023 年 9 月 1 日至 2023 年 12 月 29 日至本校傳播學院廣播電視學系擔任訪問學者。

Dr. Osamu Sakura is a Professor of Interfaculty Initiative in Information Studies, the University of Tokyo, and PI of Research Project for Science, Technology and Society, RIKEN Center for Advanced Intelligence Project (AIP), Japan. His main interests are science and technology studies, including social aspects of AI and robotics, comparative history of the reception of evolutionary theory, and cultural effects on the history of science and technology in Japan. He was also engaged in the relationship between experts and local people in the evacuation areas of the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster. Having got a Ph.D. from Kyoto University, Japan, in primatology and behavioral ecology, he taught at Yokohama National University (1993–2000) and worked as visiting scholar at the University of Freiburg (1995-96) before moving to his current position in 2000. He published several journal papers and books.

[2026-08-10NCCU Radio and Television Department to Present 2026 Graduation Showcase, In the Unfinished BetweenNCCU Radio and Television Department to Present 2026 Graduation Showcase, In the Unfinished Between 

The Department of Radio and Television at National Chengchi University (NCCU) will present its 2026 Independent Project Graduation Showcase, In the Unfinished Between, in June.

Continuing the department’s longstanding tradition of creative practice, this year’s showcase is independently curated by students and brings together diverse works in moving image, music, theatre, game design and audiovisual production. The exhibition highlights graduating students’ four years of exploration and practice in media, storytelling and contemporary issues.

The showcase consists of two main components: a Production Exhibition and a Film Festival.

The Production Exhibition will take place from June 3 to June 7, 2026, at the Exhibition Hall of NCCU’s Journalism Building. It will feature 10 projects across four categories: music, moving image, theatre and game design.

The Film Festival will be held on June 11 and 12 at the second-floor theatre of NCCU’s College of Communication. On June 14, three narrative films and one documentary will be screened at the Audiovisual Hall of NCCU’s Arts and Culture Center. An online film festival is also scheduled to take place on YouTube from June 20 to June 21, allowing a wider audience to participate in the exchange.

Titled In the Unfinished Between, the exhibition focuses on the uncertainty and fluctuation experienced by contemporary young people between becoming and not becoming, leaving and staying, and dreams and reality.

The curatorial concept suggests that people do not simply pause briefly in the process of making choices; instead, they may live for extended periods in a state of incompleteness. Unfinished decisions, unrealized ideals and futures that remain out of reach have gradually become part of everyday contemporary experience.

Rather than offering answers to struggle, In the Unfinished Between examines how struggle continues to exist. Here, “between” is no longer merely a transitional stage, but a condition in which one resides. Likewise, “unfinished” is no longer defined solely as absence or deficiency; it becomes a shared reality of life for contemporary youth.

Through different media and creative forms, the exhibition seeks to open a dialogue between the works and their audiences. Visitors are invited to reconsider their own positions and directions amid states of uncertainty and incompletion.

The event welcomes students in communication, radio and television, film and related fields, as well as all audiences interested in student productions and short films. Visitors are invited to enter In the Unfinished Between and experience the creative energy and life questions of contemporary youth.](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=1211&id=42154)

《翻轉大地：1974-1976年泰北農民的起義》

Turning the Bhumi: The Uprising of Farmers in the Northern Thai, 1974-1976

Documentary Film｜Thailand｜2024｜53 mins

 

導演 Director | Sorayut AIEMUEAYUT

主持人 Moderator｜Associate Prof. CHUNG Shefong, College of Communication, National Chengchi University

與談人 Discussant｜Prof. YAMAMOTO Yohei, Meiji University

*The film features both English and Chinese subtitles, and the post-screening discussion will be conducted primarily in English.

*影片提供中英文字幕，映後講座將以英文進行。

 

This documentary tells the emotional story of northern Thai farmers' struggles between 1974 and 1976, exploring the shifting conditions of their lives and their alliance with the student movement. The farmers, initially fighting against injustices in land management and the royal "Na Jao" rice fields system, united with students to challenge the ruling elite. This grassroots movement sparked a nationwide awareness, but tragedy struck when the farmers' leader was murdered by a collaboration of the ruling class, local capitalists, and right-wing government elements.

 

Despite this loss, the farmers' resolve strengthened, leading many to join the Communist Party of Thailand. Their struggle evolved into a larger confrontation with the state and capitalism, with many taking up arms and engaging in political education in the forests. By 1980, the introduction of the 66/23 policy forced them to abandon the fight, returning to find their communities changed and their reclaimed land now owned by others. Facing alienation and economic hardship, the farmers clung to their dreams of a just society amidst the trauma of defeat.

 

Assistant Prof. Sorayut AIEMUEAYUT

Sorayut, an anthropologist and writer based in Chiang Mai, Thailand, has dedicated over two decades to serving the Melayu people in Southern Thailand. He has authored numerous books that focus on themes of identity, selfhood, and sensory perception within the contexts of crisis and conflict. His work particularly explores the tensions between ethnic identity and nationalism through both ethnographic and ethnographical non-fiction. In recognition of his contributions, Sorayut received an Honorable Mention in documentary writing from the Office of Basic Education Commission, Ministry of Education, in 2017, as well as Second Best in Documentary Writing from the Seven Book Award in the same year. Some of his non-fiction works are currently being translated into English and Malay. Additionally, he is a columnist specializing in visual culture and serves as an assistant professor in the Department of Media Arts and Design. Currently, Sorayut is engaged in creating ethnographic films and photography projects that examine the intricate connections between public memory and personal experience, particularly in the context of Thai political violence. Sorayut was a Lisa Maskell Fellowship in Germany (2016 - 2018) and Harvard – Yenching Institute visiting scholar, Harvard University (2019 - 2020).

Title & Outline of Presentations

 

	
		
	
	
		
			
			Research and Creative Work Presentations_I
			
		
		
			
			Notations in Translation: A Transcultural Perspective on Arts 

			Assistant Professor HSIEH Chieh-Ting, College of Communication, National Chengchi University
			 

			This presentation introduces an artistic research project Transnotators, funded by

			Taiwan Contemporary Culture Lab (CLAB) and the Taipei Performing Arts Center

			(TPAC). This project invites musicians, dancers and artists to research different

			notations in different cultures. In this project, notation is redefined as “de-scription” in

			the sense of “writing-down.” The notations researched here are therefore not limited

			to music and dance notations. Rather, they include diagrams, cartographic images,

			trigrams of yin and yang in Chinese ancient writing Yi, and mysterious images in

			Taoism. In the sense that these notations not only represent different ways of “writing

			things down” but also reflect different ways of “thinking” a priori to things, they are

			also “pre-scription.” Seeing notation as “de-scription” and “pre-scription” that require“translation,” this project opens up a transcultural perspective on arts.
			
		
		
			
			Mimesis — Sound, Fear, and the Glitch of Faith

			Pimchanok YAEMSIRI, Undergraduate Student, Media Arts & Design Program, Chiangmai University
			 

			Mimesis is a digital sound experiment exploring faith, fear, and perception. It turns Buddhist moral lessons into sound and light where system errors become emotional language between belief, control, and collapse.
			
		
		
			
			WHOSE HONG KONG? WHOSE SONG? A Semi-Insider's Listening Experience of Hong Kong Identity

			LI Ho Yu, Undergraduate Student, School of Journalism & Communication, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (Exchange Student, College of Communication, NCCU)
			 

			This presentation explores the evolution of Hong Kong identity through Cantopop from the unique perspective of a "semi-local"—born in Hong Kong but raised in Mainland China. Through a musical journey analyzing three songs—Beyond's "Hoi Fut Tin Hung" (1993), Kay Tse's "Wedding Card Street" (2008), and Serrini's "True Beauty of Trees" (2021)—the presentation traces this identity from a confident collective (Beyond), through an era of collective loss (Tse), to a new generation's focus on individual self-establishment (Serrini). The presentation concludes that identity is not static or reliant on a shared past. For a "border person," belonging can be a fluid, self-created act of embracing complexity and building an individual future.
			
		
		
			
			Research and Creative Work Presentations_II
			
		
		
			
			Deconstruction and the Reconstruction of the Soul in Contemporary Art: Aesthetic, Ethical, and Existential Dimensions

			Professor/Director LEE Kuan Lian, MA & PhD Programs in Fine and Applied Arts, Dhurakij Pundit University
			 

			This paper investigates how deconstruction and structuralism—sharing common roots in rationalist philosophy—have profoundly shaped the formation of contemporary art. When rationality extends into art, it transforms artistic creation into a system parallel to scientific logic. Drawing on Heidegger’s ontology and Marcuse’s critique of instrumental reason, the study examines how contemporary art can reconstruct its spiritual dimension under the dual influence of deconstructionism and technological rationality. Through a philosophical and historical review, it traces how the artistic “soul,” once central to metaphysical and ethical aesthetics, was gradually eroded by industrialization and the dominance of reason. By analyzing representative works, this research explores how artists reinterpret the notion of the soul in aesthetic, ethical, and existential terms, revealing both the spiritual crisis and creative renewal of the modern subject. Ultimately, the article proposes a redefinition of the “soul” in contemporary art as a space where deconstruction enables regeneration—bridging the tension between rational structure and emotional transcendence.
			
		
		
			
			Rethinking Modern Happiness: D. T. Suzuki and the Practice of Daily Life

			ITO Riku, Post-Graduate Student, Place, Art, Consciousness Program, Meiji University
			 

			In this presentation, I would like to explore how happiness takes shape in  the contemporary society using D. T. Suzuki's perspectives as a guide.
			
		
		
			
			THANICA Corporate Identity

			Dr. Saran TANGTRONGSIT, Lecture of The Creative Art Department, Faculty of Fine and Applied Arts, Chulalongkorn University
			 

			THANICA is a modern Thai cosmetic brand inspired by nature and sustainability. Its name echoes the word "Botanica," while the added “H” stands for “THAI,” highlighting its strong local identity. 

			The brand repurposes agricultural waste—such as durian and pomelo peels—into valuable skincare ingredients rich in antioxidants like polyphenols and flavonoids. These ingredients help reduce cell damage and support healthy skin, with formulations developed in collaboration with experts from Chulalongkorn University. 

			THANICA targets health-conscious individuals aged 25–35 who value safe, sustainable beauty solutions. With prices starting at 490 THB, the brand offers affordable yet premium skincare rooted in environmental responsibility. 

			The brand’s vision is to create sustainable beauty from Thai nature by transforming farm waste into high-quality products. Its mission includes supporting local farmers, promoting eco-friendly production, and inspiring a new generation to embrace sustainable self-care. 

			THANICA’s visual identity reflects its brand personality—natural, minimal, and contemporary. From packaging and social media to uniforms and retail spaces, every touchpoint communicates a blend of elegance and environmental awareness. 
			 

			As a new brand, THANICA stands for more than just skincare—it represents a movement toward conscious consumption, circular beauty, and pride in Thai innovation. 
			
		
		
			
			Everyday Tasting: Why We Taste and How Cooking Teaches Us About Perception

			HONZAWA Rion, Post-Graduate Student, Place, Art, Consciousness Program, Meiji University 
			 

			This talk explores why we taste while cooking and how this act reveals our sensory awareness. Seeing tasting as an engagement between body and space, I consider how it can inspire designs that nurture the act of cooking.
			
		
		
			
			Research and Creative Work Presentations_III
			
		
		
			
			Between Anthropologist and Artist: Views from Fieldwork

			Assistant Professor Sorayut AIEMUEAYUT, Department of Media Arts and Design, Faculty of Fine Arts, Chiang Mai University
			 

			The convergence between anthropological practice and artistic creation often emerges through shared concerns with aesthetics, emotion, affect, and sensory perception. Anthropology may call this phenomenon the artistic turn, while the arts may refer to it as the ethnographic turn. Though named differently, both reflect a mutual interest in understanding and narrating human experience through diverse media—bridging cultural differences and offering critical perspectives on injustice and entrenched cultural ideologies.

			This presentation is grounded in these intersections, drawing upon my fieldwork experiences as one who moves between the disciplines of anthropology and art. It focuses particularly on audio-visual ethnography, exploring the lived realities of marginal and voiceless communities in Thailand. Through this lens, I examine the ethical, interpretive, and methodological dimensions of producing media that both documents and intervenes—serving as a bridge between academic inquiry and public engagement.
			
		
		
			
			Digital Stages of Expression:  Feminist Perspectives on Short Drama Platforms

			ZHAI Yujia, Post-Graduate Student, Place, Art, Consciousness Program, Meiji University
			 

			This presentation examines how short drama platforms in China and Japan create digital spaces where gendered perspectives, cultural narratives, and audience participation intersect. Through comparative analysis of short dramas and comment sections, it explores how women express opinions and negotiate identities within algorithm-driven environments. Adopting a media-centered approach, the talk highlights how platform design and participatory culture shape expression and reception, revealing how short video platforms both reflect and reshape gender dynamics in contemporary East Asian digital media cultures.
			
		
		
			
			Women-Made Waves: Pioneering Women in Taiwan Cinema

			Assistant Professor CHO Ting-Wu, College of Communication, National Chengchi University
			 

			This presentation extends from my curatorial research for the 30th anniversary program of the Women Make Waves International Film Festival, Inventing the Time: 30th Anniversary Special Presentation. It examines the trajectories of women’s filmmaking in Taiwan and their pioneering contributions to the island’s cinematic history. From early involvement in film production during the colonial period to the creative innovations of contemporary independent cinema, women have continually reshaped notions of authorship, representation, and visibility within a male-dominated field.

			By revisiting key moments across generations—from early industry practitioners and popular actresses to experimental and documentary filmmakers—this study traces how women have negotiated shifting political, cultural, and technological landscapes. Their works employ film as both a mode of personal expression and a form of social intervention, challenging gender hierarchies while reflecting Taiwan’s evolving social imagination.

[2025-10-13Congratulations to our alumnus Chen Yuhong for winning first prize in the New Media Art category of the 2025 Taitung Art Exhibition.Congratulations to our alumnus Chen Yuhong for winning first prize in the New Media Art category of the 2025 Taitung Art Exhibition.

 

The highly anticipated biennial art event, the 2025 Taitung Art Exhibition, announced its winners on the 22nd. In the New Media Art category, Yu-Hung Chen, an alumnus of the Department of Radio and Television at National Chengchi University (NCCU), won first prize for his work “No Longer (at) Katatipul – The Tribal Youth.” The piece deeply interprets ethnic culture through new media techniques and focuses on issues of urban Indigenous youth identity, earning unanimous praise from the judges.

 

This year marks the first time the Taitung Art Exhibition opened for international submissions, attracting 672 entries, including 22 works from foreign artists studying or residing in Taiwan. The competition was divided into four categories: Eastern Media, Western Media, New Media Art, and Three-Dimensional & Traditional Craft. After two rigorous rounds of selection—preliminary and final—80 works advanced to the final review, and the winners were officially announced following careful deliberation.

 

Chen’s work embodies the interdisciplinary spirit of new media art, while reflecting the cultural reflections of contemporary Indigenous youth in urban contexts, offering a new perspective to the Taitung Art Exhibition. The NCCU Department of Radio and Television takes pride in this achievement and looks forward to seeing its alumnus continue to shine in the art world through film and new media creations.](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=1211&id=36456)

[2026-03-11The 26th Artist-in-Residence Program Opening & Floral Art Demonstration will be heldOpening Invitation The 26th Artist-in-Residence Program: The Garden Within and Beyond

You are cordially invited to the opening of the 26th Artist-in-Residence Program, The Garden Within and Beyond. The ceremony will take place at the Art Corridor on the 4th floor, followed by a reception and a guided tour of the exhibition State of Technique (lololo Solo Exhibition) at the Art Space on the 5th floor. We sincerely look forward to your presence.

Speaker

Artist Wu, Hsin-I (Koryū ikebana School)

Location

2F Shun-Wen Lecture Hall, 4F of NCCU Arts & Culture Center

Timetable

18:30–18:55 Opening: Floral Art Demonstration byWu, Hsin-I

18:55–19:00 Opening Remarks, Artist Introduction & Group Photo

19:05–19:20 Exhibition Tour by Artists Lin Ting-Chun & Chang Hsin

19:20–21:00 Reception & Networking

Floral Art Demonstration by Wu, Hsin-I

For this floral art performance, the featured artist Wu Hsin-I draws upon the traditions of the Eigetsu Koryū (映月古流) school. In his early years, he studied under Professor Yu Bi (余碧), a master of the Eigetsu lineage, and has since accumulated over three decades of experience in floral practice and teaching. Wu has gradually developed an independent creative voice, integrating innovations drawn from multiple artistic disciplines into his work.

In addition to floral art, Wu is an accomplished painter and photographer. Earlier in his career, he worked professionally as an interior designer until his recent retirement. This diverse background has enabled his works to bring together the aesthetics of floral art, painting, spatial art, and photography into a holistic form of expression. In recent works, he further incorporates the rhythmic lines of dance, infusing still floral compositions with a sense of movement and vitality.

Milestones

1987：國立政治大學廣播電視學系於民國 76 年核准設立。院指派潘家慶老師擔任創系系主任。

National Chengchi University was approved by Ministry of Education to establish Department of Radio and Television in 1987.

Professor Pan was selected to be the 1st chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

1988：廣播電視學系成立，為全國第一個廣播電視學系，前身為新聞學系「廣播及電視組」

The Radio and Television concentration, which was part of Department of Journalism, was expanded into our nation’s first Department of Radio and Television.

1989：傳播學院成立，首任院長為閻沁恆教授，助教為黃治蘋。新聘關尚仁老師為本系專任副教授，並代理廣電系系主任。

College of Communication was established.

Professor Yen was selected to be the 1st dean of college of communication.

Huang was selected to be Teaching Assistant.

Professor Kuan substituted as the 2nd chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

1990：關尚仁老師為第二任系主任。

Professor Kuan took over the 2nd chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

1992：本系《廣播與電視》學術期刊創刊。

Journal of Radio and Television Studies was founded.

1994：教育部核准本系自八十四學年度起增設碩士班。劉幼琍老師接任第三任系主任。

Approved by the Ministry of Education, our department then created a master program since the 84th academic year.

Professor Liu took over the 3rd chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

1996： 吳翠珍老師接第四任系主任。「廣播電視研究所」正式招生，為全國第一個廣電碩士班。

Professor Wu took over the 4th chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

The Department of Radio and Television created the nation’s first master program in radio and television.

1998：系慶十週年系列活動，與中華傳播學會合辦學術研討會。黃葳威老師接第五任系主任。

Department of Radio and Television had its 20th anniversary celebration, and we held academic seminar with Chinese Communication Society.

Professor Huang took over the 5th chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

2000：舉辦「國際華語廣播電視文化性節目觀摩與研討會 」。

We held observation and seminar on nternational Chinese radio and television cultural programs.

2001：由盧非易老師兼代第六任系主任。

Professor Lu substituted as the 6th chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

2003：由陳清河老師兼代第七任系主任。「廣電製作中心」搬遷至大勇樓，並更名為「影音實驗室」。

Professor Chen substituted as the 7th chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

The Radio and Television Production Center moved to 大勇 building, and then renamed Audio-Video Lab.

2005：由蔡琰老師接任第八任系主任。

Professor Tsai took over the 8th chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

2007：由關尚仁老師接任第九任系主任。

Professor Kuan took over the 9th chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

2008：廣電二十週年系慶系列活動。

Department of Radio and Television’s 20th anniversary celebration.

2009：郭力昕老師為第十任系主任。

Professor Kuo took over the 10th chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

2011：曾國峰老師為第十一任系主任。

Professor Tseng took over the 11th chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

2013：許瓊文老師為第十二任系主任。傳播學院系所評鑑實地訪評。

Professor Hsu took over the 12th chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

2014：本院奉教育部核定，自 103 學年度起，原「新聞學系碩士班」、「廣告學系碩士班」及「廣播電視學系碩士班」整併為「傳播學院傳播碩士學位學程」。傳播學院為鼓勵多元學習，增加競爭力，採大一大二不分系招生與修課。大三前依志願申請專業主修，進入新聞系、廣告系、廣播與電視學系以完成學位。傳播學院 103 學年度正式走向「大一大二不分系」。

Since 2014, the College of Communication encourages students to improve competitiveness by learning comprehensive. To realize that ideal, the college combined three departments, which were Department of Journalism, Department of Public Relations & Advertising and Department of Radio & Television, into one Department. All students are undeclared major until their junior year of college.

2015：許瓊文老師為本系第十三任系主任。

Professor Hsu took over the 13th chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

2016：陳儒修老師為本系第十四任系主任。本校教學單位英文網頁競賽，本系獲第一名。

Professor Chen took over the 14th chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

Our department won the first place in English website competition.

2018：欣逢政大九十一週年校慶也是本系三十週年系慶。本院第一屆三系首次聯合畢展。

NCCU’s 91st anniversary celebrations and Department of Radio and Television’s 30th anniversary celebrations.

Three departments’ first joint exhibition.

2019：林翠絹老師為本系第十五任系主任。

Professor Lin took over the 15th chairman of the Department of Radio and Television.

2020：本院評鑑及實地訪評。

Department and Field evaluation.

2020/9 ：系主任林翠絹教授自109年8月1日起請辭行政職務。經改選由許瓊文教授任廣電系系主任一職至2022年07月31日。

Professor Lin Tsui-chuan resigned from her administrative position as chair of the department effective August 1, 2020. After a re-election, Professor Hsu Chiung-wen was appointed as Chair of the Department of Radio and Television, serving until July 31, 2022.

 

2022/1 ：舉辦系所友理事會議，討論本系系所友會章程修訂內容暨系所友與系辦合作事宜。

A meeting of the Department Alumni Association Board of Directors was held to discuss revisions to the association’s bylaws and matters of cooperation between the alumni and the department office.

 

2022/8/ 許志堅老師為本系第十七任系主任。

Professor Hsu Chih-chien served as the 17th Chair of the department.

 

2024/5：成立至今已有33年歷史的《廣播與電視》期刊，為因應趨勢於2024年5月更名為《亞洲廣電與新媒體研究》（Asian Broadcasting & New Media Research）（ 第43期）。

The journal Radio & Television, which has a 33-year history since its establishment, was renamed Asian Broadcasting & New Media Research in May 2024 in response to emerging trends, beginning with Issue No. 43.

 

2024/8 ：許志堅教授廣播電視學系主任兼代理傳播學院院長。

Professor Hsu Chih-chien serves as Chair of the Department of Radio and Television and Acting Dean of the College of Communication.

 

2025/8 ：黃俊銘老師為本系第十八任系主任。

Professor Huang Chun-ming serves as the 18th Chair of the department.

[Future Development](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/upload/22/doc/1880/_archive_1507_bbf3f01a.jpg)

Future Development

Mission of the Dept. of Radio & Television is to provide a diversified and multicultural environment to our students in order to increase their talent of audio dissemination of content created and media industries executed. In past 20 years, the Dept. of Radio & Television has been fostered over seven hundreds undergraduates and over one hundred graduates.

Team work, service and responsibility are hallmarks of The Dept. of Radio & Television. We want all members of the Dept. of Radio & Television to be engaged together in discovering and advancing knowledge and practice.

Career

Most of our students work at transmission companies, newspaper, radio stations, television, PR companies, Magazine companies, Advertising companies, Film industries, internet companies, and record companies after they graduate. We also encourage our students to apply study abroad to open their eyes and open their mind.

Date 2020-03-17

[Imagin Asia](http://imaginasia.nccu.edu.tw/)

The Origin of “ImaginAsia”

Imagination is a key to creation.  “ImaginAsia” was established so that students could create imaginative projects together.  It contains research presentations, culture exchange, and workshops.  Based on the common themes for these three parts, "ImaginAsia" provides an environment where students can experience international communication and cultural exploration.

With globalization, “rising of Asia” is an important trend.  However, most of the students in Asia tend to follow the Western Culture as their focal vision when they need to embrace their own culture.  “ImaginAsia”  allows Asian students to experience each other’s streets, forests and countryside, and to explore and reflect on East Asian history, relationships between civilization and nature, and current events in Asia.

Professor Suga, Kerijiro( 管 啓次郎) of Meji University, Japan and Professor Lu, Feii of National Chengchi University, Taiwan are the founders of “ImaginAsia”.  The journey started when Meiji University and Chengchi University worked together on a “Taipei : Tokyo” City themed workshop in May 2010.

    In October 2010, faculty and students from Chulalongkorn University, Thailand joined "ImaginAsia".  Besides the above-mentioned three universities, Hong Kong Baptist University and University of Southern California, also attended this workshop when it was held at Xitou, Taiwan in 2011.

    The workshop was hosted by Meiji University in Aomori, Japan the following year.  In 2013, professors and students from Japan, Thailand, Taiwan, Singapore, Malaysia, Brazil, China, and the U.S.A. were assembled to join the workshop, hosted by National Chengchi University, in Matsu Island, Taiwan.  In 2014, the workshop was held in Takamatsu, Japan to experience the culture of Japanese Islands.   A year later, National Chengchi University hosted ImaginAsia International Conference and Workshop in Taroko National Park, Taiwan.  And in 2016, members of ImaginAsia will be united again in Ayutthaya, Thailand.

 Each yeara, a main theme is named for the conference and workshop.  In the workshop, students are divided into groups of five or six to develop their presentation concept according to the main theme.  Through field research, interviews, filming and editing, students are able to create their multi-media projects in a short period of time.  Even though members come from different countries, speak various languages and have cultural differences, they always generate great chemistry within the group and (create inspiring works with profound views,  like colonialism, major disaster, nature and arts.)  create inspiring art works in respond to the history of colonialism, war and peace, humanity and natural disaster… etc.

The workshop inspires and deepens Asian youths’ social and culture awareness.  Through “ImaginAsia,” the word “Asia” is no longer a simple interpretation from the West, but a place full of diversity and multiple imaginations.

Date 2020-12-23

The Origin of ImaginAsia

‘Asia’ is neither an individuality nor an western-imagined entity; ‘Asia’ is a plurality with diversity and organic development. According to that, ‘ImaginAsia’ should not be imagined as a single entity, but multiple ImagiNations. ‘ImaginAsia’ project started planning in spring 2009 and officially launched in autumn. Taiwan, Japan, Thailand, Singapore and the UK and other countries are continually being invited and participating.

What is ImaginAsia?

‘ImaginAsia’ project aims to encourage the gazing between nations and populations through interactive and cooperative academics’ mutual teaching and researching. ImaginAsia gradually depicts a shifting, needless-to-say, amazing Asia.

ImaginAsia is a growing concept and an open organization. We welcome academics, students, and artists from every different country and culture to participate and form a group for academic, teaching, researching and creating. This project will open up conversation and gaze between different countries and different cultures through mutual or individual studying, observing, communicating, researching and creating processes.

Date 2026-05-27

With many things, you think that once you’ve thought them through, you’ll find the answer, but most of the time, you simply keep moving forward while carrying that question with you. Choices aren’t truly finalized, and situations aren’t truly resolved… but this is reality.

The theme of the class of 2026’s graduation exhibition, In the Unfinished Between, from Department of Radio and Television, National Chengchi University, aims to capture precisely this state of limbo.

This exhibition consists of two parts: a production showcase and a film festival. The production showcase features ten graduation projects spanning four categories—music, video, theater, and games—and will be held from June 3rd to 7th in the News Building Exhibition Hall; The film festival will take place on June 11th–12th at the Theater and on June 14th at the Arts and Culture Center’s Audiovisual Theater, featuring screenings of three narrative films and one documentary. Faculty and students are all welcome to attend!

[小圖](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/22/doc/1767/web_news_2.jpg)

以往的作品呈現與討論都在校內，容易侷限在同溫層中，這次能到校外放映與交流，甚至是到國外，對我們而言是非常難得的機會。在這次的影展中，我們欣賞到了很多特別的作品，因為彼此的國情不同、文化不同或是語言不同，每個作品都展現出各自豐富的樣貌，而讓我們收穫最多的，則是在每次的映後交流，創作者和觀眾分享理念、回答觀眾的問題、吸取觀眾的意見，能在欣賞完作品的當下和觀眾做立即交流及接收回饋，在創作上提供了非常大的幫助，很感謝廈門大學的師生舉辦這個盛會，讓來自各地的師生能夠認識彼此和交流想法，也感謝在這幾天擔任地陪的莊同學，帶我們認識廈門大學的周邊環境與享用美食，最後感謝政大提供的一切資源與幫助，這是個非常難忘的經驗。

日期：2018-01-01

[_archive_2208_9a6bdd0e](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/22/doc/1762/_archive_2208_9a6bdd0e.png)

這次很榮幸在廈門大學的協助與安排下，能與眾多畢製組別的同學一同參加第四屆兩岸大學生影像聯展，也很幸運地《倒數七天》被選為開幕片的其中一部影片。在這幾天的交流中，除了觀賞許多來自各地的作品外，也特別感謝主辦單位細心的安排，於眏後讓製作團隊上台分享關於作品的理念，並且開放大家討論不同的議題，透過這樣的方式，不僅促進了更多影像上的交流，也收穫了更多不一樣的創作概念，著實讓我們學習到了許多。

其中，有一兩部令我們印象深刻的作品， 一部是來台灣的《迷海龜途》，紀錄了海龜與海洋污染間的關係，透過紀錄片，大家不僅更加深入理解了關於海洋污染的議題，對環境保育有了不同的反思，也看了創作者在創作中的堅持與努力，是一部非常值得省思的紀錄片。而另一部則是來自 中國的《獨路》，敘述了關於文化大革命命的議題，藉由廣闊的景色與寫實的鏡頭， 表現革命下小人物的孤獨與心酸，是一部非常特別且有意義的影片。

很開心能藉由這次的交流，和不同地區的同學分享創作，每一部影片都是每位創作者的結晶，從中不僅看見了大家對影像的熱愛與堅持，也看見了很多未觸及到的議題，希望未來能有更多類似的交流活動，讓大家能有彼此學習和分享的機會，也期望大家能繼續創作出更多優秀的作品。

最後再次特別感謝廣電系的友芳助教、帶團的適芳和力昕老師，以及協助相關交流活動的廈大的同學與老師！

title: Detail?fid=4134&id=1765
text:
[:::](http://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=4134&id=1765#accesskey-l)

[:::](http://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=4134&id=1765#accesskey-c)

日期：2018-01-03

播放影片的大禮堂

在大禮堂前的自拍

第一次聽到力昕老師宣布這屆的畢製同學有機會到廈門大學與當地的同學交流時，我從沒想過會是我們這組。幸運的，我與郁程帶著熱騰騰的作品坐上了飛往對岸的班機。

在出發前，力昕老師告知我們因為是臨時將我們的作品加入參展的行列，因此不會出現在主要的播映廳內，但是，還是希望我與郁程可以在另外的連播廳跟看過我們作品的同學有所交流。

當下說不失望的假的，這樣等於失去了與當地的老師、同學互相交換意見的絕佳機會。但往另外一方面想想，我們依舊可以藉著觀看當地同學的作品獲得想法、觀點，這會是一個瞭解對岸的同學到底都在想些什麼的直接方法。

世事難料，沒想到我與郁程的作品經由力昕老師的幫忙，被搬上了大螢幕。雖然作品本身礙於記錄時間的限制以及田野的範疇，說它是紀錄片，我覺得更像是一則專題報導。固然，我仍然覺得題材本身是具有意義的，值得讓我們再思考教育與階級複製之間的關係。

與台灣一樣，身在中產階級以上的他們無法透徹的瞭解高等教育的僵化與不合理性，或者說，我們避免去談論這個複雜且敏感的議題。看到對岸的同學對這樣的題材有所想法、啟發，我覺得這就足夠了。我與郁程並不期待影片本身能夠呈現的多豐富與意涵深遠，對我們來說，「看見」這個議題才是我們想要達到的效果。

最後，我覺得中國的學生與台灣的學生在拍攝的題材上，有非常大的不同。也許是因為台灣類似的議題被討論的太多，大家都在尋找新的議題深入研究。反之，中國的同學們似乎喜歡拍攝一些風土民情、愛情故事，在影片的中心思想上屬於中規中矩的範疇。這在大量的觀看紀錄片與劇情片之後非常明顯，只要有議題上比較新穎或批判的，大部分都來自於台灣的同學。

對此，我覺得能夠在像台灣這樣自由、開放的教育環境下激發思想、獲取知識實在是太幸運了。

謝謝力昕老師與廣電系辦以及所有畢製的參與者給予我們這次交流的機會，希望廣電系與廈門大學這樣的交流能夠繼續下去。

title: Detail?fid=4134&id=1766
text:
[:::](http://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=4134&id=1766#accesskey-l)

[:::](http://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=4134&id=1766#accesskey-c)

日期：2018-01-16

[小圖](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/22/doc/1766/web_news_2.jpg)

一、兩校關係

廈大和政大的影展交流據所知至少有三年了，這不僅是學生製作的討論平台，也是各地師生與學生間思想交流的難得機會。

相較於本校廣電畢展，廈大的規模是相當大的、形式也較為正式傳統。我很榮幸被指派為開幕式的政大代表主持人，在到達會場時被現場氛圍震懾，坐滿人的禮堂約三層樓高，受邀大學來自中國各省以及香港與台灣。

我沒有正式主持的經驗，風格相當綜藝，但廈大同學們和兩位男主持人非常樂於助人，其一是當地廣播主持人、專業主播，其二是念傳播學的同年廈大學生，都是校內典禮主持的老手，為我做了簡單的正音訓練和心理建設，也就順利成就了有趣的經驗。而與之在後台順稿的時候聊起兩岸關係，我問得很小心，倒是對方說地淘淘不絕。就像所知的，年輕一代對兩岸關係不再有那麼緊繃的想法了。

二、策展

廈門大學的策展規模相當大，活動量和人力也驚人，但在細節方面難免未能注意周全。舉例說明：放映人力不夠。僅安排學弟妹坐在角落按播放鍵，且有中途切斷影片的問題。

三、觀影方式

QA之中，能看出兩岸同學對影像解讀有所不同，最明顯的就是，中國同學總是喜歡問導演開放式結局的真正結局，必須是一個明確唯一的答案。而連續兩部台灣的片都是開放式結局，中國同學不禁脫口：「啊？結束了？又是開放式結局？」顯得相當不喜歡此一手法。這似乎也反映了兩岸學生的思想模式，台灣帶來的創作多追求答案以外的更多討論，而中國同學不喜歡模稜兩可或不確定性。

title: Detail?fid=4134&id=1763
text:
[:::](http://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=4134&id=1763#accesskey-l)

[:::](http://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=4134&id=1763#accesskey-c)

日期：2018-01-01

[小圖](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/22/doc/1763/web_news_2.jpg)

很開心也很榮幸能在適芳和力昕的帶領下，和畢製同學們一起帶著作品到廈門大學參加影展，並和來自中國各地的同學交流。這是我第一次參加像這樣的交流活動，其實蠻有意思的，可以看到和我們來自不同環境、生長背景的大學生所拍出來的作品，欣賞他們的長處，檢視我們的不足，但同時也更珍惜我們生長在台灣所帶給我們在創作方面的自由。

其中北京電影學院的學生所創作的短片《回家》，取材自中國北方的少數民族，因為拍攝技術以及題材的稀有性，讓我對他們的作品印象深刻。另一部我很欣賞的短片是來自台灣台藝大的《野潮》，記得班上一起去交流的同學們也都很喜歡，可以說被我們視為畢業製作的模範，無論劇情技術表演各方面都表現得恰到好處，而影展結束後也的確陸陸續續傳來了該部影片得了數個影展的消息，鼓舞了我們也激勵了許多正在拍片路上努力的人們。我想交流就是這樣，互相觀摩切磋，檢討、學習而後成長。很感謝有這樣的機會讓我們能到廈大交流。

title: Detail?fid=4134&id=1759
text:
[:::](http://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=4134&id=1759#accesskey-l)

[:::](http://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=4134&id=1759#accesskey-c)

日期：2018-01-01

[_archive_2222_9b064956](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/22/doc/1759/_archive_2222_9b064956.jpg)

首先，想先感謝廣電系鼓勵我們積極參與這次的鳳凰花影展，也感謝廈門大學給予了寶貴的機會，讓我們能和兩岸四地的新秀們交換彼此的作品與意見，這樣的機會在我們的大學生涯中真的非常可貴。

這次參加鳳凰花影展我們不只得到了作品的回饋、大量創作的欣賞，更看到了文化衝擊，三者都讓我們覺得格外的充實。首先，在播出作品後，各地的師生給予了我們莫大的鼓勵與指教，除了提供我們許多有建設性的意見之外，也給予了我們許多其他文化立場的觀點；看了影展中的其他影片，也吸收到了很多不一樣的思考與影片的創作手法，更讓我們感受到在廣電系所見到的創作能量遠遠不夠，世界真的很大，我們早已習慣了台灣的同溫層，少見到其他多元的創作，因此這次的交流讓我們與其他創作者擦出了許多火花，有許多想法值得更深層的討論。

最後，是對於中國大陸的文化探索，在台灣，對於中國大陸有著許多偏見與刻板印象，這次的廈大交流是我們第一次踏上中國大陸的土地，也是第一次親眼見到中國大陸的光景與文化，有許多與我們所想的不一樣，有許多遠遠超前我們的發展，還有許多遠遠落後我們的部分，這樣的消長與高下讓我們有了很多體悟與思考，也深刻體認到跳脫舒適圈與同溫層的必要性，因為看到、聽到、經歷到更多不同的文化與生活，才能有更豐富開放的價值觀和思考模式。

這次的鳳凰花影展我們感受到很多用心與努力在其中，尤其是開幕式中的介紹影片等等，都能讓我們感受到滿滿的誠意，但是有些小錯誤與瑕疵還是要注意一下，有幾個建議想送給鳳凰花影展，希望播片的時間能變成更多天，每天不用看這麼多，對認真參展的人而言，其實是滿疲憊的負擔，排片時間也不要太早，以免觀眾過少，無法促成熱絡的互動，實在可惜，最後就是放映場地，希望能找到更合適播片的場地，希望鳳凰花影展在明年也能順利舉辦，並且更好更盛大，成為更多兩岸四地的學子們的創作交流平台。

參加鳳凰花影展能得到來自兩岸四地的意見與聲音，讓我們能有機會思考如何讓作品被更多人理解與感動，這對我們來說是很難得的經驗，畢竟對創作者來說，能得到回饋是格外欣慰的事。

text:

日期：2018-01-01

[_archive_2221_fb174d3b](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/22/doc/1760/_archive_2221_fb174d3b.jpg)

畢展還沒開始，就能先到海外的學校播片，真的是非常難得的機會。在製作動畫時，其實沒有想到會有機會讓這麼多人看到我的作品，在播片的當時滿緊張的。廈門大學非常大，人也非常多，開幕式時播片的場地非常大，開幕表演也很精彩，尤其是廈大還特別剪輯了所有影片的介紹特輯，影展辦得非常盛大，讓人印象深刻。

 

在小教室的播片，雖然動畫片的播片時間比較早，來的人還是比想像中多，而且非常認真、踴躍地提出意見，能夠聽到同學對各個片子的看法與討論，我覺得相當值得，也算是趁畢展前試試水溫，回台灣後還能做個最後修正，很棒的機會！雖然播片的教室沒有階梯差，人員進進出出有些干擾，有些非中文的片子字幕都被擋到，因而錯過好好了解劇情的機會，又因為要播的片子太多，壓縮到很多和創作者互動的時間，真的有點可惜。期待之後的影展能越來越好，除了提升觀影品質，也增加更多讓創作者和觀眾互動的時間！

自己平常比較少關注大陸的影視作品，這次到厦大可以一睹廈大的學生製片，覺得非常開心，也因此得到很多靈感的啟發。覺得大陸的拍攝手法相當成熟，也看得出來設備和製作成本都不錯！廈大的校園的建築很有特色，學校裡還有個湖，坐在湖畔聊天打發時間非常舒服。學校招待我們的餐點也很豐盛，可惜我一到廈門就因為水土不服腸胃一直不太舒服，也因此沒機會在影展結束後跟老師同學們一起到酒吧喝酒慶祝。不過後來有跟同學離開廈大到街上走走，去了學校附近的寺廟參觀，還有些同學去體驗了按摩，我們則去吃了當地學生推薦的麻辣燙，非常好吃，也算是有走到完成廈門的觀光行程！非常感謝這次學校提供這麼好的交流的機會！

text:
[:::](http://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=4134&id=1768#accesskey-l)

[:::](http://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=4134&id=1768#accesskey-c)

日期：2018-01-16

[小圖](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/22/doc/1768/web_news_2.jpg)

早便聽聞，系上學長姐在畢業製作作品完成之際，會有一個難得的機會到中國的廈門大學進行作品交流，這樣的平台來自港台中三地的學生可以展映作品，對於學習中的創作者來說無疑是重要的機會。

很開心廈門大學提供了一個這樣的機會讓政大的學生能夠參與其中，能夠在中國、香港、澳門和其他台灣學校的同學面前，有交流互動的機會。在華語圈裡，孜孜不倦的創作者不乏少數，但是能夠看到學生作品的機會很少，誠屬難得的活動，廈門大學的老師與接待同學也很熱情的招呼我們，帶我們參觀校園周遭，甚至有小酌之夜。

影展分成不同影片類型的單元，分成兩天作展映，每一個影片單元都會延請兩到三位、來自不同學校的老師進行映後講評。劇情片的部分香港同學的作品表現很令人驚艷，在形式上和風格上都很穩健，也對於劇本下了不少功夫，還記得有一個同學分享他的精神指導是侯孝賢導演。這次本校推出了不少紀錄片作品，更巧的是，我的畢製指導老師適芳老師正是我的作品《告別二式》的講評老師。同個時段有一支紀錄片作品，講述自閉症孩童在中國的收容機構會面對什麼樣的處境，直面的紀錄讓人佩服創作者的勇氣及中立，處理敏感議題的困難常讓鏡頭語言流於感情用事，但是這支作品調度是中，很是難得。

也在適芳老師的映後點評得到很重要的提醒，讓我有了新的方向在真正的畢業展覽前為作品做調整。在整場交流下來，收獲之多遠超過我的預期，也因為跟接待的廈大同學交流，漸漸對於中國大學生現在的思想與處境有了更多的認識。謝謝學校，謝謝力昕老師、適芳老師、亞維老師這樣不辭辛勞地為我們在畢業展覽之餘，打點這麼多特別的活動與機會。也謝謝系辦行政上的諸多協助。如果學弟妹也能有這樣的機會，我想我會特別推薦他們積極爭取，能在學生時代得到越多的分享與討論都是有助益的。

沙灘上的前浪之眼看交流影展

畢展前夕的初夏，我們一團十來人在力昕與適芳的帶領下飛往廈門，參加廈門大學主辦的兩岸大學生影像聯展。被海包圍、可遙望遠方鼓浪嶼與金門的小島，有與台灣相似的面貌。但此處的人們與我們熟悉的環境截然不同，從負責接待我們的同學口中得知，這次影展籌備人員除了來自學校的新傳系所外，也包含校內電影社的同學，且許多參與辦理活動的學生都還只是大一、大二的年紀。雖然辦活動的是年輕的後輩，但在活動中看到的文宣、紀念品、接待等事務的面貌俱足，讓面臨畢業大關的我直感慚愧。

在實際交流上，我們看到中、港、澳、台四地許多院校的作品，兩部令人印象深刻的影片是台藝大學生的《野潮》與山西傳媒學院的《獨路》。這兩部劇情片，前者描述西部沿海漁村孩童的生命經驗，後者描述山西特有的文化在文革時期的變化，兩者在劇本描述的經驗與創作者的位置上，都恰好對應一近一遠。近者，與我們可算是同存於一座城市的邊緣，我們卻繞了一大圈，在緣際會下在外地才能見到這樣一部精彩的作品；遠者，如果不是幸而能受邀來此，我們如何接觸在台灣，或在我們一定範圍的生活中不可見得的生命經驗？

驚艷之餘，不僅也開始思考自身經歷過的大學四年，回望自己曾參與或眼見的製作課程或實習單位，雖然每學期都有一兩個大大小小的展演活動，但跟廈大的鳳凰花影展相比，我們的展演活動像是散落各處的碎片。在課程的映演活動中，會參與的人除了課程同學與親友外，不太能接觸到其他群體，在實習單位的活動中，情形換成組員、演員、學長姐構成觀眾主力。不同的活動之間，有課程與實習單位等身分為界，分化了人群，雖然也有人知道要四處參與不同活動以汲取各種經驗，但我認為這始終是消極的想法，更積極的是去想我們能不能創造一個連結不同影片類型、不同程度創作者的舞台，提高展演活動中創作者互相交流、學習的機會。

也許可以說甫結束的畢製最接近前一個想像，但回到前面驚艷我的遠近二部影片，我想問：「我們與其他人的連結在哪裡？」這一兩個學期，隔幾棟樓的中文系請來業師連結實際策展、校內有學生跨越校系舉辦特定主題的影展連結青少年觀眾、在海峽一端有連結四地共十餘所學校的大學生交流影展。這些活動得以成形仰賴預算、人力等各種外在條件，但驅動這些條件被湊齊的，是我們對於展演活動如何連結他者的想像。最後我要大膽諫言，與其每年投入大量人力物力參與校內例行競賽換取所謂向心力，重視現有的展演活動聯合起來與往外連結的可能，並在使之可能的過程中磨練自身，才是身處大山深處的我們的首要之務。

法國/特魯瓦

交換與旅遊

克羅埃西亞

Groupe ESC Troyes

特魯瓦高等商學院

家裡的廚房

書桌

床

學校大廳

交換學生報告

          我就讀政大傳院的廣電系。我希望能在法國完成碩士學位，因此出國交換主要是為了學習法語、了解法國及歐洲的文化以及嘗試沒有接觸過的課程，如果情況得宜則外出旅行。於我來說，選擇交換的國家比選擇城市或學校還重要，時間上兩個學期也可能優於一個學期，這完全取決於我的動機與目的。本篇心得大致以上述幾個面向來書寫，將個人經驗分享給有需要的人，至於技術性的攻略則著墨較少，畢竟網路上的資料非常多，只要加以篩選整理即可獲得有用的資訊。

 

一、選擇國家與城市：法國/特魯瓦

 由於我並非法語系出身，在出國前的法語程度大約只是A1，如果希望快速達到申請碩士的門檻B2，那麼直接把自己丟到法國或法語系國家是最快的。再從時間考量，比起待一個學期才剛混熟就得離開，兩個學期的時間則相對充足。因此在選擇志願上，法國的所有學校自然排在前面，比利時法語區、加拿大魁北克和其他選項則放在後面。至於最後學校落點在特魯瓦（Troyes），則是幾個選擇的濾網篩選之下的緣分，稍後會繼續說明。

 

法國是個偏向中央集權、獨尊巴黎的國家。從城市規模來看，巴黎大都會區一千萬人口，然而第二線城市馬賽、里昂、土魯斯馬上降至一百～兩百萬人，三線城市則在一百萬人以下。從這種城市分級結構來思考，選擇法國後的下一個問題，便是要住在巴黎或是不住在巴黎。法國的物價其實不太受到大、中、小城市的影響，巴黎家樂福超市的售價可能和小城市家樂福的售價差不多，巴黎觀光區的消費價格當然不在一般生活的討論範圍之內。真正有差的是房價，巴黎的租屋價格高昂、品質欠佳卻經常競爭激烈，一般留學生、交換生的房租大約落在500~800歐之間，端看屋況、房型、區位和大小等因素來決定。然而，大巴黎以外的城市房租大致上可以降個150~250歐元左右。

 

我居住的城市是法國東部，香檳-亞登大區（Champagne-Ardenne）、奧布省（Aube）的首府特魯瓦（Troyes，法語念ㄊㄨㄚ4聲），是個中世紀發展出來的貿易小鎮，在法國城市排名中約20名～30名、人口10萬左右的小城市。我住在市中心，外面就是H&M、法雅客Fnac等逛街商業區，離火車站走路7分鐘，房價加上電費大約400歐（我的CAF房屋補助一個月92歐，所以真實房價大約是300歐）。

 

特魯瓦城市影片：[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QnUXw89cjQw](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QnUXw89cjQw)

我自己非常喜歡特魯瓦步調悠閒的簡單生活，在市區隨便走都會遇到同學或認識的人，也許緩慢的節奏在年輕人眼裏是過度放鬆，但對於來自亞洲擁擠都市的人來說卻難得清淨。然而小城市有優點亦有缺點。特魯瓦沒有機場也沒有高鐵TGV，聯外方式是搭一個半小時的火車往西北到巴黎或是往南至其他城市，例如葡萄酒鄉勃艮第的首府第戎（Dijon）。此外，也可搭乘法國國鐵營運的巴士（OuiBus）至臨近城市，例如香檳的世界酒鄉蘭斯（Reims）。若是要搭高鐵則必定要在巴黎轉車，交通時間必須拉長。

 

位在巴黎的交換學校是很搶手的，學校成績和語言檢定高分的同學可以考慮。巴黎是法國的政治、經濟、文化中心，交通便利且資源豐富，各類活動精彩萬分帶動著世界趨勢。然而，在全球化與資本消費主義的影響之下，世界各大城市的差異性被削抹，巴黎與倫敦街上開著一模一樣的連鎖品牌商店，城市之間越來越像也越來越無聊。大城市的高物價、高房價以及通勤的時間/金錢/精神成本，再加上過度擁擠的城市生活，同時還要費神留心治安等問題（在巴黎地鐵裡不要只會睡覺和玩手機，在觀光景點不要只會拍照打卡，你會死。），如此模式常使人非常疲憊。

 

巴黎雖然是我非常有興趣的文化與藝術重鎮，但在交換之前我的法語不佳，在語言的屏障之下，我無法真正了解巴黎或法國的核心精神與內容，因此巴黎對我來說並非必要之選。我希望居住在一個大家都不太講英語的地方，迫使自己在日常生活中使用法語，又能觀察平民百姓的生活方式與習慣，沈浸其中照自己的進度接觸新知與體驗文化。

 

因此，在安排志願時，不在巴黎但靠近巴黎的幾間學校（還是想去巴黎走走，但不想住那裡）就是我的思考重點。北方大城里爾（Lille）大概是不錯的選擇，雖然天氣很差、非常濕冷，但是城市規模適中，交通上坐歐洲之星到英國倫敦只要1.5小時，坐高鐵到比利時布魯塞爾1小時，到首都巴黎大約1.5小時，真是神位置。然而，最後結果落在特魯瓦也是可接受，雖然她有時過度寧靜、缺乏生氣，法東的天氣又很詭譎多變，但總體來說還是滿意的。十個月內，我前往巴黎旅遊數次，總共加起來約莫待了30天，即使沒住巴黎也將她摸清了大部分。

 

二、交換與旅遊

 先說題外話的真心建議。如果交換只是為了在歐洲旅行，選擇交換的季節及交換的城市便非常重要！以我的經驗來建議，歐洲旅遊的好時機是春季交換（二月至六月），這段時間的歐洲氣候將從二、三月的寒冷轉為四、五月的舒適，再到六月的乾熱（卻不像台灣的濕/悶/熱）。二、三月仍可從事滑雪、賞雪、看極光等冬季旅遊的項目；四、五月是歐洲最棒的春天，綠意盎然、鳥語花香，到哪裡都可以舒適旅遊，而且遊客少，票價、房價亦較便宜；六月歐洲開始炎熱，可以從事海邊的水上、水下活動，更是北歐的旅遊好季節。

秋季（九月至一月）大約從十一月開始轉冷，十二月至隔年一月是最冷的時候，住在西、北、中、東歐的民眾必須長袍、圍巾、手套和毛帽加持，只有南歐還稍微可以住人。此時白晝縮短夜晚加長，高緯度北歐國家則日照稀少，南歐國家卻把陽光當貨幣在使用，整個歐洲的許多旅遊景點將關閉致使旅遊不便。有錢的歐洲人逃到熱帶，留守歐洲的人多半心情鬱悶、脾氣暴躁、缺乏笑容、體重增加，只能殷殷期盼聖誕節，藉由過度購物與消費來發洩。因此，想旅行的人選擇春季吧！除非你只為了聖誕節。

 

為了旅行的交換計劃，則須注意所居城市之地點與交通情況。旅行最重要的就是交通便利，想要地理位置居中不如選擇德國有機場的中型城市，一個月房租也許200~300歐而且位於歐洲中心到哪裡旅遊都很近。想要便宜的話，推薦選擇東歐國家的首都，相信有非常多前輩會推薦捷克、波蘭。我有朋友選擇在立陶宛的首都維爾紐斯交換，一個月房租住學校宿舍只要90歐（豈不比台北市便宜？），住品質好的公寓也只要140歐，當地物價更是比台灣還要便宜，首都有機場因此旅行不成問題。試想，如果交換一學期，整整五個月中有四個月都在旅行，因此沒住在你交換學校所處城市，那麼還需要選擇巴黎這種一間套房月租600歐的城市嗎？白繳2400歐的房租卻沒有使用不是很蠢嗎？

 

從歐洲的消費水平來看，北歐、瑞士、盧森堡>英國倫敦>荷蘭、法國、比利時、都柏林>德國、西班牙、義大利、奧地利>葡萄牙、匈牙利、希臘>捷克、波蘭、斯洛伐克>東歐、東南歐剩餘國家。其中每個國家的觀光勝地、首都、大城市當然物價會更高。對於那些大半時間都在旅遊而不在住處的交換生來說，交換到哪個國家可能不是重點，選擇房價低廉、地理位置不要太偏、對外交通便利的城市則更為重要。然而，如果你真的只是要旅遊，何必交換？？歐洲自助旅行三個月就很夠了還比交換更簡單、更便宜。

 

三、選擇學校：特魯瓦高等商學院

當然，並不是想選擇去哪裡就可以去哪裡，還是要看學校的位置。政大的法國姐妹校跟其他學校的選擇比起來是非常的多，但主要是商學/管理學院，如果是人文社會科學大致就幾間公/立綜合大學，至於我有興趣的傳播、電影相關學校則幾乎沒有。因此，在沒有修課、學分抵免壓力的情況下，我對於前往哪間學校就讀則無太大執著，十之八九會被分到商、管學院，那麼既來之則安之，學習我以前沒接觸過的領域也是一種體驗。

 

特魯瓦高等商學院（Groupe ESC Troyes）是1992年設立的私立學校，據說一年學費7000歐元。學生少，大家容易認識，在學校也容易見面，學期制度和政大相似，約一千一百多名學生，國際學生約一百人。學校範圍很小，面積大約是政大總圖、商院、 研究大樓那一區面積的總和，但樓高大約只有3~5層，其中的新大樓應是2015年才蓋好，一樓的中庭走廊是學生活動區，有桌球、室內簡易版羽球、撞球可以玩，還有學生社團自主管理、營運的咖啡零食吧，今年又增加大螢幕提供學生玩PS4和Wii。

一堂課的時間是一個半小時！學校老師頗愛點名，有學生只來第一節，翹第二節，但老師每節都點名。這方面德國朋友說比德國還要嚴格。監考也很嚴格，要核對學生證、不可帶包包，我的歐洲朋友們真的是很愛作弊，但我還是很愛他們。

 

學士學位－3個

國際管理學院INBA, School of International Management （我的學院）

國際旅遊學院EMVOL, School of International Tourism （我主要修課的學院）

藝術學院ESAA, Graduate School of Applied Arts （應用設計科系，法語授課為主）

 

除了學士班，還有上述科系的碩士班。這所學校以商管、旅遊見長，法語授課和英語授課各占一半，碩士班幾乎是全英語授課，但藝術學院主要以法語授課。學校師資有部分是產業界的專家、業師，公司經理、杜卡斯集團旗下餐廳的經理、洲際酒店經理、奢侈品集團LVMH的市場經理也可能是你的老師。做學術研究的理論老師也是有，負責基礎專業課程，整體來說比較少。

 

此外，這所學校提供交換生一個學期兩次的法語課程，在來交換之前會在線上的系統先做分班測驗。一次是開學初期8天，一天6小時，上、下午各3小時的密集課程，另一次是學期間，一周三小時共上8周的一般課程。師資因人而異（我聽過很有趣的也聽過很無聊的），我幸運的都遇到算會教的老師，如果遇到不適合自己的班級，可以儘量試試換班或想辦法解決，一切的學習需要自己主動，台灣的媽寶教育在法國不適用喔！

 

特魯瓦高等商學院的行政效率不差，有問題主動寄信問（注意學校人員的上班時間）都會得到解答，如有重要資訊也會以信件主動告知。住宿的選擇方面，學校會有合作的私營套房宿舍或合租公寓，一切都在入學後學校提供的線上系統中可查閱，不但有照片可以看屋況，還有資訊知道租金、押金、地址、面積、格局、傢俱等等，在選擇房子時注意學校、住家、市中心彼此的相對位置和距離，搭配網路地圖可得知週邊生活機能，再衡量自己是否滿意。

我和德國、吉爾吉斯的室友住一間67平方公尺的公寓，位於市中心非常方便。房東Brunet夫婦人非常好，太太是學校的西班牙語老師，他們不占房客便宜但也不讓自己權益受損，遵守法律、有原則、尊重房客權益和隱私，房屋出現問題只要一個簡訊一通電話則馬上回應，處理的速度非常快，可惜的是完全不會英語，所以兩個不會講法語的室友也必須透過我溝通，反映問題或繳納電費賬單也由我負責。

 

房東要求退房時要將房屋打掃乾淨（契約有規定），恢復得到房屋時的情況。然而，德國和吉爾吉斯室友比較不拘小節，也較不重視收納，平時無定期打掃的習慣，多半是等到邀請朋友來家裡party前，會應急地拿吸塵器將公共區域清掃ㄧ次。室友們都比我早退房，但沒有將公共區域清掃乾淨，因此我在退房時自己將整間房屋打掃乾淨，浴室、廁所、客廳、廚房、傢俱都大掃除。檢查房屋時，我因此受到房東的讚美，讓我不必分攤損壞傢俱的賠償費用（浴室流理臺因為不當使用、沒有清潔而發霉損壞，有張椅子破掉，幾顆燈泡壞掉。）。

 

三、學業篇

我交換至特魯瓦商學院的隸屬學院是國際管理學院（INBA, School of International Management），然而我修最多課的學院是國際旅遊學院（EMVOL, School of International Tourism），主要是因為我發現商學的課程我實在沒太大興趣，頂多修了行銷與品牌相關的課程，財務金融、會計那類則沒有接觸。我選擇的課程都是英語授課，班上八成～九成是法國本地學生，其餘是國際交換生。

這所學校的課程多半速戰速決，時間短則15小時，兩個星期內找三天上完，接著安排考試或繳交報告。時間長的從24~48小時不等，要上兩、三個月，考試多、作業多，大部分是法律、商學課程。之所以必須這樣彈性地安排課程，是因為至少有七成的老師來自業界或其他學校，他們像是出差一樣（有位加拿大老師自稱Flying Professor）從國外或其他大城市來到特魯瓦小鎮上課，待個幾天上完課又必須前往其他國家或城市的學校授課，因此課程安排上必然配合老師的檔期，而不像政大每週有固定的行程表。課表總是千變萬化，經常調課或是前一天臨時取消，要不老師在交通上遇到問題（例如罷工），要不就老師太忙必須改變行程，總之必須每週確認下週的行程以及上課地點。我喜歡速戰速決的課程，讓我一段時間只需專心在1~3門課的內容即可，接著在我記憶猶新時完成測驗或報告，較沒有在政大期末考時卻忘記期初究竟上了什麼的問題。

 

起初我在網路上找不到這所學校的課程，完全是等到開學前一週才從學校開放給我行政/教學/選課作業網站（類似iNCCU＋選課系統，非學生進不去），得知究竟有開什麼課。相較政大老師們在選課時提供的詳細教學大綱，特魯瓦的課程介紹多半寫得籠統，上課日期和時間也可能有所出入，若遇到有一些時間衝堂則允許曠掉幾堂課，真的不行再跟負責課務的行政人員退選。總之，主動尋問並說明自己遇到的問題，能修課就是能，不能也就接受。以下條列我兩學期上過的課程，因為老師很容易換因此內容對於後來的學生沒有太大參考價值，僅供參考。

以下分享在法國上課的情形。我上的都是英語授課，上課的情形也只是一種樣貌，無法代表全體，企圖找尋代表法國全體的描述也毫無意義。因此，勿以商業周刊或主流媒體那種「歐洲學生都如何如何積極努力、勇於發言，台灣學生請加油」的視角，自我殖民於歐美已開發國家的教育想像之中。

 

英語並非法國人的母語，所以上課時會發言的法國學生多半無法以英語長篇大論，僅以片段句子表達重點或回應老師，至於在法語授課的課堂中，學生是否會更積極發言我不得而知。我班上的法國學生在課程上的投入程度接近於我在政大課堂中遇見的同學們，端看老師的授課內容/方式是否吸引學生。如果老師講不清重點、內容無意識鬼打牆或充滿廢話，台底下大約9成的法國學生會打開電腦做自己的事情，逛網拍、唸下堂課的考試、上臉書、打LOL、打電動、做作業，就跟台灣學生一樣會利用時間或是打發時間，桌上立滿電腦的畫面蔚為壯觀。然而，當老師上課有趣時，學生會放下手邊工作熱情地回應老師。學生喜歡輕鬆充滿歡笑的上課氣氛，有時候太愛聊天、打鬧嬉戲也會被老師制止。以上或許是法國商院學生的某種特質，但勿自動腦補到所有人身上。

 

我班上的法國同學在英語報告時，經常照著PPT直接唸一遍，和沒受過報告訓練的學生差不多，老師多半鼓勵學生注意與觀眾的眼神交流、用自己的話表達不要照PTT唸。法國學生不害羞上台，也不會發生不願意第一個報告的彆扭「讓賢」行為，有的人會大方耍帥/搞笑地完成報告，有的人會懶惰地敷衍完就下台，也有同學以有創意的方式呈現雖然未必有深度，一種法國麵包養百種法國人。基本上，要是你的英語口語還算流暢、發音清楚，就可以勝過我班上一半以上的法國同學。

 

四、法語、英語與法國文化

歐洲的文化政策差異，導致歐洲的英語普及程度有兩種不同的發展。在電影、電視劇、新聞等影視產品中，有一派是維持原音配本國字幕，另一派走的是國語配音無字幕。在美國強勢主導全球影視產業、英語作為強勢語言的情況下，前者的政策導致國民從小耳濡目染英語發音的美國電影、影集、電視劇而對英語不感到陌生；後者則將所有外語取消，無論是電影院裡的電影，或是電視上的新聞一律配上本國語言。

 

法國的文化政策屬於後者，除了巴黎或大城市的電影院可能有原音配法文字幕，其餘地區的電影院裡都是法語配音、無字幕的電影，而電視節目和新聞只要是法語發音就無字幕，國外電視劇、影集則全配上法語。因此，法國人的英語除了在學校教育會接觸以外，在日常生活中除非主動尋找，否則很少接觸，這導致一般法國人對英語的語調、發音、用字習慣、詞句結構都相對陌生，在和外國人突然以英語對話時常無法應對，而不願意說英語。以葡萄牙來比較，該國的文化政策施行前者，因此雖然葡萄牙語和法語同樣源於拉丁語系，但葡萄牙的英語普及程度卻高於法國。

 

法國人不願意（或不會）說英語，間接導致對待本國人和外國人有嚴重雙重標準的刻板印象（某程度來說是事實），常令外人感覺高傲自大。我的法語程度，可應付朋友間的閒聊，以及買東西或銀行辦事情之類的日常生活所需，我也儘量以法國人那套強調尊重、厚禮數的行為模式與他們相處，因此我在特魯瓦遇到的法國人之中，八成是態度良好、樂於幫忙、能解決我的疑問或是告訴我接下來該怎麼做，但也有兩成的機率遇到無熱忱、表情呆滯以及擺爛的服務，甚至敷衍的官僚態度。

 

在我無法清楚以法語表達意思或是理解對方時，也遇過法國國鐵的客服人員、銀行行員、熱心路人主動以英語耐心說明並協助我。我的朋友就沒這麼幸運了。由於她對法語實在沒轍，必須以英語溝通，因此她遇過許多法國人一聽到英語就直接搖頭、說NO或聳肩裝傻，搞得她時常被氣瘋。雖然如此，年輕人普遍英語程度較好，我也遇到英語很厲害的法國同學。當然，亞洲人在巴黎通常會被法國人當成觀光客，所以可能會轉變成兩成良好、三成普普通通、三成隨便敷衍、兩成惡劣──這種看天氣與他本人心情而隨機決定的態度，和海底針一樣很難撈而無法猜測。

 

法國禮數，我個人覺得比台灣還要重視。在法國走進任何一家店，無論服飾店、酒吧、麵包店、超市、餐廳……，看到店員、警衛、安檢人員都會主動問好（Bonjour或Bonsoir），主要是告知店家「我進來了喔！」，讓彼此都知道對方存在，像是客人進到主人的家裡，一切有禮貌互相尊重。

 

不同的消費習慣和禮儀文化常導致外國客人（多半來自東亞）被恨、被歧視、被差別待遇。以下列出可能讓法國人討厭的情況：進到店裡無視店員的存在不打招呼，像幽靈飄進去直衝商品；結帳的店員跟客人打招呼卻沒獲得回應，法國人超級恨打招呼不回；店員在跟顧客介紹說明時，顧客只顧著低頭看商品，沒聽對方說話而也不看著店員（有些朋友習慣低著頭，不習慣看別人的眼睛），店員就會覺得自己很沒尊嚴而心情很差；走進餐廳不打招呼、不告知人數直接衝進去找位子坐下，並且催促給菜單或上菜；去別人家吃飯、party卻兩手空空沒有帶酒或食物存心白吃白喝。

 

反正，法國人心情不好就很容易使出差別待遇，或是傲嬌擺爛翻白眼。若是顧客以為大聲就會贏，態度跺跺逼人叫經理出來就會達到目的，那麼完全會獲得難忘的反效果，因為經理出來只會袒護員工。但是，我也遇過愛硬凹的法國朋友，明明是自己的問題但是藉口一大堆彷彿自己沒錯，投機、貪快、小聰明者比比皆是（大家都是人，小姦小惡俯拾皆是），此時如果能得理但饒人，讓愛面子的人有台階下，通常還是可以成功溝通、解決問題，藉此提升自己的危機處理能力以及情緒商數。

 

在此祝大家和法國人相處愉快。

 

五、您對於國合處辦理與該締約學校之間的交換細節，如甄試、薦送、聯繫等事宜，您有無任何建議？

我在申請的過程中都很順利，這是我第二次申請交換，也因為一些機緣跟不少行政大樓的處室接洽過，我認為政大的行政效率並不差，行政流程和規則也都算寫的清楚，有問題可以直接詢問，一般來說不會有大問題。在此謝謝相關老師、行政人員的協助與努力。

至於有本屆的同學（104學年第一學期）覺得六分鐘的面試成績不公平，或是兩位面試老師的評分差異過大，我認為稍微有幾個觀察點提供思考。首先，六分鐘的面試占了三分之一的評分比例，是否面試時間短暫而導致無實質意義？我在面試中只被要求自我介紹，以及說明為什麼要去法國，答畢則結束面試。以上的問題在我的被審資料中都有寫到（都是很基本的問題），其實並沒有提供給面試官更多有關學生的資訊。

 

但願是我的理解錯誤，我只能假設評分老師是就學生的儀態、口語表達能力來給分。六分鐘對一個學生的觀察，可以佔評分比例的三分之一、與在校成績和語言檢定成績相等嗎？對此，我是抱持著懷疑的態度。我知道因為面試人力有限，技術上不可能將時間延長，然而六分鐘的面試對照所佔評量成績，也不合比例原則。因此，個人覺得面試的佔分比必須降低，或是以其他評估方式替代。

日期：2013-04-27

[小圖](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/upload/22/doc/1729/web_news_2.jpg)

學校與生活環境

Hochschule für angewandte Wissenschaften Neu-Ulm，簡稱HNU。位於德國西南部的NeuUlm，與南德大城Ulm只有一橋之隔，生活機能完整，無論是超市、傳統市場、服飾、醫藥等等都能在這兩個城中找到。兩個城內的公車網絡也相當綿密，一般大學學生都會購買一種叫Semester ticket 的票，主要的功用就是能在半年之內無限制搭乘Ulm及NeuUlm城中的公車（其實公車的網絡也有延伸到周邊其他小城市），價格為99.5歐。對於在這搭一趟公車就要2歐來說，仍相當值得購買！

HNU是一所商科專業的應用科技大學，校地面積與政大相比的確相當迷你，大約只有四棟大勇樓的大小。但其實裡面圖書館、學生餐廳、電腦教室一樣不缺，設備也很新穎。但我認為來到HNU最開心的事情莫過於，這裡的國際事務處對國際學生相當友善且提供許多幫助。在抵達德國前就會有Tutor與你聯

絡，告訴你該注意的事項。抵達之後的Orientation program 也協助我們將延簽、銀行戶頭、選課、等等的問題安排妥當，星期五也會舉辦不同的Party增進國際學生的感情。在學期中有時也會舉辦小型的出遊計畫。舉例來說，十月時我參加在鄰近城市的高空繩索課程，對於在台灣從未參加過類似活動的我是非常新奇的體驗。同時也在攀爬繩索時和一群朋友們建立起了革命情感！ 

學校雖然不大，卻有許多社團和活動！時常能在學校的⼀樓大廳中看見藝文展覽或者是學校爵士樂團或者搖滾樂團的表演。聖誕節時學校籌劃了一個小小的聖誕市集，聽朋友說是學生自組的活動，會將收益捐給慈善機構。而每個學期還會有一次由老師組織的國外參訪活動，但當然活動進行都以德文為主。本來我在今年有被邀請參加五月英國倫敦的參訪活動，但因為在那段時間已有別的計畫因此沒辦法參加，但如果未來學弟妹能把握這個機會，會是相當難得的體驗。整體來說，這所學校的風氣自由且活潑，學生的自主性相當高！

課程學習

由於HNU是一所商業導向的學校，英文自然也成為相當重要的授課語言。所以在這邊有許多英文課程可以選擇，但全部都是與商管相關的課程，這點需要在交換選校時考慮進去，建議可以上HNU的網頁大致了解英語授課的課程有哪些。上學期我選了〈跨文化管理〉、〈中國現況研究〉、〈全球化〉這三堂課。〈跨文化管理〉的報告讓我印象深刻，因為我必須與國際學生一起合作報告，語言是障礙之外，彼此的報告習慣不同也是需要克服的問題。但很幸運地，我的三位韓國組員相當負責且認真，經歷報告之後，我們四個人培養了深厚的情感，成為生活上相互扶持的好友。大致上，我認為課程並不會太重，主要都是老師講課為主，上課分組報告。不過，這或許跟課程有關，因為這學期我選的國際傷法語歐盟法規就比較嚴格，老師時常要求我們要記清法規。

而對交換學生最重要的德文課程這裡也有提供，在開學前有兩星期的密集班，開學後則是每星期3小時，不過只提供到A2的程度。但HNU有與位於Ulm的大學合作語言課程，因此若德文程度較高的話，可以選擇Ulm的語言課程，無需另外付費。此外Ulm的語言課程中有些英語課程並不一定是以語言教學為主，而比較像是英語授課的專業課程。像上學期我選修了〈希區考克電影分析〉，全班只有六個人，每個禮拜討論一部希區考克的電影，輪流由學生帶領討論。為了要能在討論時清楚表達想法，每次討論前都必須認真準備。且由於Ulm大學是醫藥及生物科學為主的大學，有些同學會以心理學或神經科學角度分析電影，這是在人文為主的政大較少接觸的觀點，使我受益良多。

社團

到HNU之後，意外發現它們有新組成的合唱團，喜歡合唱的我得知消息後立刻加入。在這個合唱團的體驗相當新奇，因為團內只有12個人，女生就占了9個，男生只有3個。雖然聲部並不平均，團中有3個人是學校的老師和員工，指揮不會說英文。但每次在那個小小的合唱室裡，有了音樂，身分和語言不是阻礙。平時在路上遇到，大家都會向我都會很熱情的打招呼，不會說英文的指揮，即使衝著我直說德文，還是能感受到他的真誠。這份溫暖，讓我仍有在每個寒冬夜晚前去練唱的動力。而學期末我們在聖誕市集以及學校的年度聖誕聚餐上的表演，收穫半年的練唱成果，是我相當美好的回憶！

柏林影展

在二月時我透過陳儒修老師的介紹，有機會在柏林影展的Film Market 擔任台北市電影委員會的攤位工作人員。對我來說，應該是到德國交換以來最珍貴的一段經歷。在Film Market 裡面我看見的是電影的另外一面，那是一個屬於發行商和影展策劃人員的世界，這與我以往接觸的製作層面相當不同。在擔任攤位工作人員的那幾天，有機會接觸了來自美國的亞洲電影雜誌總編輯、柏林影展Film Market的總策劃、世界各地片商、獨立製作的導演、台灣的各個發行商及Buyer。每天到攤位上看著台灣發行商和各國片商斡旋，將台灣的片子一部部送上國際舞台，同時聽著Buyer們評論著今年影展的參展電影，即使只是聆聽對話，都是一種享受。而台灣的發行商們也很願意跟我分享這個行業的工作內容，這些都大大開闊了我的眼界。而當然我也在影展期間觀賞了短片競賽單元，從以前只看網路上或者DVD的影片，到現在能進入電影院看著螢幕，參與放片後的對談，真實感受到影展的氛圍，那是一種舒服且令人著迷的感受。謝謝台北市電影委員會給我這樣的工作機會，當然更要感謝陳儒修老師的引薦。

這段旅程我受過許多人的幫助，其中我最要感謝同是廣電系的蔣沂吟學姊，她是在我上一學期到HNU的學姊，我從申請到安頓好全部都靠她幫忙，一回國就要跟我解說學校的事情，真的很謝謝她！

其實到國外交換並沒有一種令你成長的魔力，所有的經驗都必須靠你伸手去抓、認真去吸收。建議想出國交換的學弟妹們，先想想自己有什麼一定要在國外完成的目標，那怕只要一個，都能讓這段交換的旅程充滿價值了！
